chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated to us, from his father, from Amr ibn Jami', from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his fathers, peace be upon them,

that he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his Family, said: Learn the Qur'an in its Arabic, and beware of accentuation (nabr) in it. That means the Hamz (glottal stop). And Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: The Hamz is an addition to the Qur'an, except for the original Hamz, such as the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'So they do not prostrate to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the Heavens and earth', and such as the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And when you killed a person and disputed over it'.

key_terms.النَّبْر: Excessive or distinct accentuation in recitation
key_terms.الْهَمْزُ الْأَصْلِيَّ: The original, essential Hamz inherent in the Qur'anic text

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between original Hamz and added Hamz in Qur'anic recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the scholarly distinction between the essential hamz (glottal stop) inherent in the Qur'anic text and 'nabr,' an artificial accentuation or elongation introduced by reciters. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the original hamz is preserved, excessive or incorrect hamz constitutes an addition to the divine revelation, underscoring the precision required in Qur'anic recitation (tajwid) to maintain textual integrity.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Amru bin Jumay’, from Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, from his fathers, peace be upon them,

that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Learn the Qur’an in its Arabic, and beware from accentuation with it. That means adding Hamz to it. Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, also said: The Hamz is an addition to the Qur’an, except for the original Hamz, such as the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «So they do not prostrate to Allah, who brings out what is hidden in the Heavens and earth» [27:25], and such as the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And when you killed a person and disputed over it» [2:72].
